chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) stood upon the grave of a man from the Shia and said: 'O Allah! Grant companionship to his loneliness, and comfort his solitude, and settle upon him from Your mercy that which makes him independent of the mercy of anyone besides You.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for the deceased in the grave according to Imam Abu Ja'far?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication by Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the Shia practice of visiting graves to intercede for the deceased, specifically emphasizing spiritual comfort during the intermediate state (Barzakh). The prayer underscores the concept of divine sufficiency, asking Allah to grant mercy so profound that the deceased becomes independent of all other creation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on direct reliance on God's mercy in the afterlife.
